To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) porcine thyroid follicles can be reconstituted in vitro in the presence of thyrotropine; (2) thyrotropine induces the formation of new follicles; (3) the follicular pattern is stable for at least 3 wk in the presence of TSH; and (4) the follicular structure is maintained even in the absence TSH.
porcine cells can be maintained for at least 4 wk in a serum- and thyroxine-free culture system and that they are responsive to acute stimulation by thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in vitro.

thyroid cells in primary culture can be kept in a resting state in serum-free, chemico-defined medium, and that the cells respond to thyrotropin with increased iodide uptake, increased thyroglobulin synthesis, and increased export into the medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a serum-free, chemi- cally defined medium for the culture of porcine thyrocytes.
the development of a new model for the study of thyroid function in vitro.
the development of an in vitro model that allows the study of the regulation of thyroid function in the absence of extracellular matrix and in the absence of the presence of thyrotropins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
porcine cells can be maintained as highly differentiated follicular-associated cells in a chemically well defined, serum- as well as thyrotropin- free medium.

thyroid cells in culture are able to maintain their differentiated functions, even without the support of thyrotropins, and that they can be stimulated by this hormone to increase their iodide transport activity.
the porcine thyroid follicle can be reconstituted from freshly isolated cells in a chemically and hormonally well-defined system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
porcine cells are more responsive to thyrotropin than human cells.
